Its AC inlet is on the FRONT, at the left end; the rear carries only three fixed fans.","format":1,"gaps":[{"reason":"needs-photo","scope":["front"],"wanted":"WHETHER THE BOTTOM RJ-45s HAVE LAMPS. They are drawn bare, as seen, and L76 stands. A close photograph of one stack settles it.","what":"bottom-rj45-lamps"},{"reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["rear"],"wanted":"WHICH WAY THE FANS BLOW. The only size source, stated once per variant and identical."},"copper-speed-spelling":{"confidence":"measured","note":"THE COPPER PORTS SAY speed 1g, NOT 1000base-t. The first draft spelled the four combo jacks' speed 1000base-t, which the DCIM exporter does not type - it knows (rj45, 1g) - so all four fell out of the NetBox and Nautobot exports without a word; the export listed 30 interfaces where it should list 34. 1g is the library's spelling for a copper traffic port. The MGMT jack is exported only through an overlay, by the exporter's own rule for role: mgmt, whatever its speed says."},"csfp-is-an-sfp-cage":{"confidence":"registry","note":"THE CAGES ARE SFP CAGES; CSFP IS WHAT GOES IN THEM. The Compact SFP is a module form that fits the standard SFP cage, which is the whole of its point - so the cages are std/sfp-ganged@1 (two-high stacks, the registry's 15.0 row pitch, measured here at 14.96) with media sfp and a csfp attr, the same decision the AMX3200 made for CFP2-DCO."},"figure-choice":{"confidence":"measured","note":"Gate 1. The base's front elevation is cropped flush - ink fills all 1000 px - and reads -1.96% on aspect against 440/44, so its box was not trusted until features said so. THEY DO, THREE WAYS. At 2.273 px/mm (440 mm across the image) the QSFP+ opening measures 18.48 mm against the ganged-QSFP 18.50, the RJ-45 cavities 12.3 against the jack's 11.91 cavity, and - most tellingly - the two rows of every SFP stack sit 14.96 mm apart against the registry's measured 15.0 belly-to-belly SFP row pitch. So x scales at 2.273 and y uses the same scale, with the elevation's 102 rows holding about 0.9 mm of margin. THE REAR IS WORSE: +5.26% on aspect. Only its x positions are used."},"left-end":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"THE POWER INLET IS ON THE FRONT. An IEC C14 inlet at the left end with its rating printed below it ('~100-240 V; 50/60Hz; 3 A'), a ground stud with its symbol beside it, the Edge-core wordmark and the model name above, and the legend '(dot) SFP LED indicator' explaining the dots beside some port numbers. A honeycomb vent row runs along the top of the port field."},"numbering":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"READ OFF THE ELEVATION, and each CSFP cage carries TWO numbers. Under the bottom cage of the first stack the legend reads '1' and '3'; above its top cage '2' and '4': a CSFP module presents two bidirectional fibre ports, so 24 cages give the datasheet's 48 ports - 'by inserting a CSFP transceiver that supports two BIDI fiber ports, each port can connect to two CPE/IAD devices, so the total number of physical ports is 48'. Stack k carries 4k+1 and 4k+3 in its bottom cage and 4k+2 and 4k+4 in its top. EACH CAGE DECLARES THE TWO INTERFACES IT PRESENTS - csfp-1-3 carries `interfaces: [port-1, port-3]` (roc-ops/Portrayal#443) - so the DCIM export lists port-1..port-48 and the cages themselves are not interfaces. The switch's silicon has both ports whether or not a module is seated, which is why they belong to the cage and not to the optic. With the SFP+ as port-49..52 and the QSFP+ as port-53/54, the export is port-1..port-54 - the 54 in the model number. THE COMBO JACKS ARE copper-45..copper-48. They were port-45..48 first, which is exactly the ids the twelfth stack's CSFP interfaces need; both connectors are real and a DCIM must cable each, so the copper jacks take their own names and each carries `combo-with` its fibre interface. L105 holds interface ids apart from placement ids. Ports 45-48 are COMBO: the twelfth stack's cages and the four RJ-45s beside it are bracketed together on the faceplate, and the datasheet lists '4 RJ-45/2 CSFP' combo ports, 'Either RJ-45 or CSFP port can be chosen at a time'."},"port-lamps":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"EACH STACK'S BELLY STRIP CARRIES FOUR TRIANGLE LAMPS, down-up-down-up, which is one per logical port and says whose it is: a down-arrow points at the bottom cage and an up-arrow at the top, and each sits on the same side as that port's printed number - 1 left and 3 right below, 2 left and 4 right above. So the lamps are assigned, not guessed, by the two things the faceplate itself says about them. The SFP+ stacks carry one arrow per port the same way, and the QSFP+ stack a down-arrow, four small windows and an up-arrow; the four windows are drawn and not given to a port."},"rear":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"THREE FIXED FANS behind honeycomb guards punched in the rear panel, rotors showing through, centred at 121.6, 239.5 and 351.1 mm on x. The rear elevation is +5.26% off aspect, so its vertical positions are read on its OWN vertical scale (95 rows for 44 mm, 2.159 px/mm) rather than the front's: the guards run y 2.3-32.4, high on the panel rather than centred on it, which is what the elevation plainly draws. A first draft centred them on the chassis height by assumption, and the matched-scale comparison showed it wrong. They are not trays - nothing in the datasheet calls them hot-swappable, and the rear shows no handles or seams - so they are drawn as the panel's own perforation, not as modules."},"rj45s":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"THE TOP COMBO JACKS SHOW LIT LAMPS AND THE BOTTOM ONES SHOW NONE. The elevation draws two green windows in the upper corners of the jacks for 46 and 48, at 307.5, 318.5, 326.9 and 338.3 mm, and nothing at all in the corners of 45, 47, the console or MGMT. The top jacks are the lamped part; the rest are drawn bare because that is what the metal shows, which leaves three Ethernet jacks on a bare part and L76 standing - see the gap."},"sources":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"ONE DOCUMENT, and it covers two machines. ecs4530-54csfp-datasheet (the ECS4530 Series data sheet) is a two-column comparison of the ECS4530-54CSFP and the ECS4530-54CSFP-DC-I; the staged -I datasheet is byte-identical. There is no quick start guide. Page 3 carries four elevations 1000 px wide - both variants' fronts and both rears - and three product photographs of each variant are staged at 489 px, too small to measure (1.1 px/mm) but enough to say which rear belongs to which front: the base's fans read at 28%, 54% and 79% of the width in its own rear photograph, which is the rear whose fans are at 121.6, 239.5 and 351.1 mm, and not the -I rear, whose fans sit elsewhere. Issue #341 warned 'expect to reach Gate 1 and find nothing measurable'. That turned out pessimistic: the page-3 elevations measure, and the next note says how
